bullets.title: FOMC June: Hawkish shift — 9/18 dots pencil in 2026 hike, markets price 38bp
bullets.body: Fed held rates at 3.50-3.75% unanimously but June SEP showed 9 of 18 members projecting at least one 2026 hike; core PCE revised sharply higher to 3.3% (up 0.6pp). Chair Warsh dropped forward guidance entirely, emphasized 'price stability' 13x vs. labor markets 3x, and announced task forces on comms/balance sheet/inflation framework. Markets moved from pricing 0.8 to 1.5 hikes by year-end; 2Y yields +13-15bp on day. Morgan Stanley maintains Fed on hold through 2026 (core PCE at 3.0% q4/q4).

bullets.title: Mag7 & Software sold off post-FOMC; Semis bucked trend on AI demand
bullets.body: SPX -1.2%, NDX -1.0%; Mag7 down 2.5% as a source-of-funds. Software basket -2.9%, IT Services -3.6%. Semis +1.4% led by memory/CPU on persistent AI chip demand; JPM notes semiconductor market cap-to-revenue surpassed 6x (double Mag7), warning that elevated positioning and rising volatility risk VaR-shock-driven selling similar to early June. JPM estimates $165B of equity selling/bond buying from quarter-end rebalancing.

bullets.title: META -5.4% on departure of AI executive Emily Dalton Smith
bullets.body: META was among the weakest Mag7 names, dropping 5.4% following reports of the departure of AI executive Emily Dalton Smith, compounding the broader post-FOMC risk-off selling.

bullets.title: AMZN -3.5% on FTC lawsuit risk over misleading advertisers
bullets.body: Amazon fell 3.5% on reports of a possible FTC lawsuit alleging it misled advertisers, with potential billions in civil penalties. Non-store retail (e-commerce) category in May retail sales data showed +9.9% YoY growth, reflecting Amazon and Walmart share gains.

bullets.title: GOOGL -2.4% on UK CMA order; but MS bullish on GCP monetization via $50/watt GPU deal
bullets.body: GOOGL fell 2.4% as UK CMA ordered improvements to search. Morgan Stanley sees GOOGL's rental of ~110k GB300 GPUs from SpaceX at ~$50/watt as signaling higher GenAI ROIC — if GCP monetizes incremental GW at $25/watt, MS estimates 27% upside to '27 growth estimates vs. current models implying only $14/watt incremental revenue. GOOGL also partnering with HSBC on AI across 200+ use cases expecting ~$100M net benefit.

bullets.title: INTC +3.5%: 18A-P process node enters early production, meets timeline
bullets.body: Intel surged 3.5% after announcing its 18A-P chip entered early production, meeting timeline expectations. This was the standout single-stock positive catalyst in the tech sector amid a broad post-FOMC selloff.

bullets.title: ANET: KeyBanc raises PT to $200; 1.6T switch + XPU demand drives 28% '26 growth intact
bullets.body: KeyBanc raised Arista's PT to $200 (from $178) after company meetings, citing the new 1.6T switch (7060XE7) with rack-scale design available 4Q26/1Q27, and XPU scaling from hyperscalers as a structural tailwind for open networking vs. Nvidia's closed ecosystem. Revenue growth guided ~28% in '26 and 25-30% in '27; non-GAAP EPS could reach ~$5.00 in '27. $3.5B AI revenue target for '26.

bullets.title: NVDA: $80B buyback + $0.25 dividend raise; 22V flags capex impact on S&P cash return ratio
bullets.body: NVDA announced an $80B buyback and raised its dividend from $0.01 to $0.25. 22V Research notes S&P 500 cash return ratio hit its lowest level since post-GFC/COVID as incumbent tech pivoted to capex — if cash returns stay at 1Q levels for 5+ years, fair value would be ~15% lower. COHR also signed LOI for $50M CHIPS Act funding for a $650M NVDA expansion at Sherman, TX to double manufacturing and quadruple wafer capacity.

bullets.title: MRVL +5.5%, WDC +4.4% in Canadian session; memory stocks on parabolic move
bullets.body: Marvell Technology and Western Digital saw outsized gains (MRVL +5.5%, WDC +4.4% in Toronto) as memory/DRAM stocks continued their parabolic move driven by persistent AI chip demand. JPM flagged semiconductor VaR shock risk given elevated positioning but noted demand fundamentals remain intact.

bullets.title: AAPL raising product prices amid memory chip supply crunch
bullets.body: Apple is reportedly raising product prices due to memory chip supply constraints rather than demand-driven factors — a potential margin pressure signal and confirmation of the AI-driven chipflation dynamic Morgan Stanley highlighted as an emerging inflationary force.

bullets.title: INTU: Citi Buy ($591 PT); QBO price hikes 13-24% effective 8/1, FY27 revenue tailwind
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on Intuit with a $591 price target (119% upside from ~$269). QBO price increases of 13-24% take effect August 1, 2026, bundling AI features, expert services, and industry solutions. Net tailwind to FY27 QBO revenue despite some bundling offset from add-ons previously sold separately; valuation at 20.4x FY27 PE.

bullets.title: HOOD +8.8% on SEC tokenized-stocks proposal under innovation exemption
bullets.body: Robinhood surged 8.8% after the SEC proposed allowing tokenized stocks under an innovation exemption. The S&P Exchanges/Data index fell 3.6% on related CFTC threats to exchange revenue, with CME dropping 3.5% additionally on CEO Duffy's retirement announcement.

bullets.title: FOXA acquires ROKU; NFLX denies Lionsgate bid; PSKY/WBD gets China regulatory approval
bullets.body: Fox Corp announced acquisition of Roku (FOXA down for third straight day). Netflix denied interest in acquiring Lionsgate, sending LION -6.2%. Separately, Paramount Skydance received Chinese regulatory approval for the Warner Bros. Discovery transaction.

bullets.title: GEV +6.8%, NNE +5.4% on Bernstein initiations; FSLR -3.6%, ENPH -4.9% on negative ratings
bullets.body: Bernstein initiated coverage framing a 'once-in-a-generation' US energy transition driven by AI/data center demand: Outperform on GEV ($1,206 PT) and CEG ($296 PT); Underperform on FSLR. SMR/nuclear broadly gaining while solar ETF fell 3.5%.

bullets.title: SHOP: UBS Neutral; Shop Campaigns a 2035 call option, Payments pricing adds 50-250bps margin
bullets.body: UBS maintains Neutral on Shopify but highlights Shop Campaigns revenue doubling in 2025 with merchant adoption tripling — a modest ~low-MSD% of gross profit contribution in 2028E but high-teens% blue-sky in 2035. Shopify Payments pricing changes on premium/corporate/AmEx cards add ~50-100bps GAAP gross profit growth and ~100-250bps adjusted EBIT growth in 2026. Long-term algorithm: 15-21% GMV CAGR and 15-20% gross profit CAGR through 2035.

bullets.title: MS raises conviction on C, CFG, COF ahead of June 24 stress test
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley sees the 2026 Fed stress test (results June 24) as potentially catalyst for lower Stress Capital Buffers: Citigroup's SCB improved 70bps over two years to 3.6% but remains above peer floor; COF and CFG both carry highest SCBs at 4.5% but credit trends improving significantly (COF card NCOs down ~110bps). All three rated Overweight; dividend announcements expected in weeks following results.

bullets.title: ACN -5.8% ahead of earnings; CTSH downgraded to Hold at Berenberg (PT $59 from $81)
bullets.body: Accenture fell 5.8% ahead of its BMO earnings report. Separately, Cognizant was downgraded to Hold at Berenberg with the price target cut to $59 from $81, underscoring broad IT Services weakness (-3.6% sector on the day).

bullets.title: T names new CFO (Jennifer Biry, Jan 2027); stock down 3.1% post-FOMC
bullets.body: AT&T fell 3.1% after naming Jennifer Biry as new CFO effective January 1, 2027, replacing retiring Pascal Desroches. Separately, T is limiting employee AI usage due to cost concerns — a notable data point on enterprise AI cost management.

bullets.title: Restaurant traffic: CAVA +23.9%, CMG +9.3%, SBUX +1.4% YoY; MCD -3.8%, WING -5.2%
bullets.body: Citi weekly traffic data (week ended 6/14) shows total restaurant footfall contracting 1.9% YoY (improving from -3.1%). Fast Casual accelerating at +3.2% YoY. CAVA led all concepts at +23.9% and CMG +9.3%, while Starbucks +1.4% (accelerating 170bps). McDonald's -3.8%, Wingstop -5.2%, and Wendy's -14.1% were notable laggards.

bullets.title: GRMN: KeyBanc HQ visit incrementally positive on wearables/aviation; rates Sector Weight at 22.7x FY27E
bullets.body: KeyBanc came away incrementally positive from a Garmin HQ visit, citing low-double-digit wearables market share gains vs. Apple's ~50% using battery life and proprietary OS as moats. Auto OEM contracts at historically high per-vehicle pricing. New Thailand facility targeted end-2026 to potentially double capacity. However, maintaining Sector Weight given 22.7x FY27E valuation vs. historical 17-28x range.
